[spoiler=Battle of the Bouj Canal] Dear Diary he puts on his personal book. However after a long moment of thinking, no thoughts come to mind and the entry is left blank. The soldier sighs, with sounds of his own worries and burdens creeping from his voice and his own eyes.
He pauses for a moment, before reaching into his pocket for his rations. A can of refried beans and corn, very well seasoned and spiced. Kaaganika wears the most wondrous of perfume, it is said. The soldiers rests against a crumbling wall, and tries to enjoy his food, taking his mind elsewhere, to happier sands.
This is very abruptly ended by an explosion nearby, the destruction of yet another building, forcing more and more people to rely on ground level trenches, reinforced by the rubble of said destroyed buildings. For this was the sad reality of those fighting at the Bouj Canal, which had very quickly become Erenes Battle of Verdun, very akin to trench warfare previously taking place somewhere around a century ago.
By now the Islamic rebel groups had for the most part united into the SILF (Shamatian Islamic Liberation Front) upon realizing that even with their alignment in religious beliefs, Baladullah well and truly stood for peace.
The frontlines had mostly stabilized, forming an easy to draw line of rebel and syndicate territory. This only made the fighting more brutal and costly, as commanders on both sides would lead charges into enemy territory, facing extremely high casualties for a few miles of land at a time.
The Bouj Canal, a tributary of the lake, ran through most of Southern Kaaganika, and was especially important thanks to its economic influence and strength in Kaaganika, and tens of thousands of soldiers would end up being lost over little more than water. The battle would last 5 long, grueling months because of this.
The reason these commanders were doing this is because they knew they could. Kaaganika had a mandatory military service policy in place, which gave it ann impressive military presence for its size but unfortunately put a large portion of the countrys population at war. The Kaaganikan Syndicalists would end up finally winning due to simply having more industrial capability and keeping most of the weapons, ammunition and food at the start of the revolution. The victory is a major national achievement and is used to spur the people to support the reunification of the nation.
Kaaganikan casualties: 95,000~
SILF casualties: 40,000~
[/spoiler] [spoiler=View of the Kaiser-Sikirsk War] The Kaaganikan government had recently taken power at around the same time the Kaiserreich-Sikirskan war had begun. The Kaaganikan syndicate has been busy with battling the rebels in the south of the nation, however the nation has been leaning more towards the Sikirskan government due to their proximity to the warring nation, and the bond between Nestor-Sikirsk and the Kaaganikans was now very special, to say the least, considering their situation. Kaaganika, among others, was very aware of the Kaiserreichs reputation of claiming completely non Kaiserreich lands and people as their own, and is currently very distrustful of them, however no aid was sent to Sikirsk for obvious reasons. Currently, Kaaganika has no plans to join the IPEA due to their situation as well as a lack of trust in an organization of such ragtail, insignificant nations, according to Ayoub Tazi, the leader of Kaaganika, as well as being aware that as long as nobody was going to get involved, the Kaaganikans had the better chance of winning their civil war.[/spoiler]
